questions.q: Match each mechanism of drug-induced hemolysis on p96 to its classic culprit drug(s) — 1) Autoantibody mediated (drug-independent) 2) Autoantibody mediated (cold autoimmune hemolysis) 3) Immune complex mediated 4) Adsorption (extravascular) … A) Quinidine, rifampicin and isoniazid B) High-dose penicillin C) Methyldopa (m/c) and procainamide D) Lenalidomide
questions.exp: Drug Induced Hemolysis on p96: Autoantibody drug-independent = Methyldopa (m/c) & Procainamide; Cold autoimmune = Lenalidomide; Immune complex = Quinidine, Rifampicin, Isoniazid; Adsorption = High dose penicillin (Extravascular). (Book p96)

units.title: Immune Classification & Coombs Test
units.sec: Classification of Immune Hemolysis & Coombs Test
units.guide:
Immune hemolytic anemia divides into autoimmune (warm IgG, cold IgM, PCH IgG/Donath–Landsteiner), alloimmune (HDN IgG, transfusion reaction) and drug-induced.
AIHA presents as rapidly progressive extravascular hemolytic anemia; the Coombs test differentiates immune from non-immune anemia.
Direct Coombs (DAT) uses polyvalent anti-human Ig to detect RBC surface antibodies (3+/4+ agglutination), followed by monovalent anti-IgG and anti-C3d.

units.title: DAT Subtyping & Warm vs Cold Etiology
units.sec: Monovalent DAT Subtyping & Warm vs Cold AIHA Etiology
units.guide:
Anti-IgG+ / C3d± indicates warm AIHA (or drug-induced if negative); Anti-IgG– / C3d+ indicates cold AIHA, PCH (DL test+) or drug-induced (Ab+, DL–); multiple transfusions cause false-positive Coombs.
Warm AIHA (m/c, IgG, 37°C, subacute 1–2 mo) is 50% idiopathic or secondary to SLE/CLL/HIV, autoimmune diseases (RA, PAN, IBD, scleroderma) and drugs (cephalosporins, drug-independent α-methyldopa).
Cold AIHA (IgM, 0–4°C, chronic indolent) is idiopathic cold agglutinin disease or secondary to Waldenström's (MYD88), lymphoma, infections (IM, EBV, CMV, Mycoplasma) and lenalidomide.

units.title: Warm vs Cold: Pathogenesis & Smear
units.sec: Warm vs Cold AIHA: Pathogenesis, Clinical Features & Smear
units.guide:
Warm AIHA: splenic macrophage Fc receptors mediate pan-agglutination and extravascular destruction in the spleen, causing anemia, spherocytosis, moderate splenomegaly, jaundice and urobilinogen (+).
Cold AIHA: IgM agglutinates RBCs in peripheral extremities (causing acrocyanosis) and Kupffer cells mediate predominantly extravascular destruction in the liver (minimal intravascular).
Warm AIHA smear shows variable spherocytes, fragmented/nucleated/polychromatic RBCs; cold AIHA smear shows agglutinated RBCs.

units.title: AIHA Treatment, Evans & Spherocytes
units.sec: Warm vs Cold AIHA: Treatment, Evans Syndrome & Spherocytes
units.guide:
Schistocytes are fragmented/helmeted RBCs; warm AIHA is treated with steroids (1 mg/kg/d × 4 wk) + rituximab (100 mg/m² weekly × 4) with slow taper, and rituximab/cyclophosphamide/MMF/splenectomy on relapse.
Cold AIHA is treated with rituximab (best prognosis); C3b activation occurs in cold agglutinin disease.
Evans syndrome (warm AIHA + thrombocytopenia) associates with CVID; spherocytes also occur in hereditary spherocytosis (uniform), G6PD deficiency, transfusion reaction and CuSO₄ poisoning.

units.title: PCH & Drug-Induced Hemolysis
units.guide:
Paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria (PCH) causes Coombs-positive acute intravascular hemolysis: polyclonal IgG binds RBC P-antigen at 4°C and lyses cells at 37°C (Donath–Landsteiner test, tertiary syphilis, conservative Rx).
Drug-induced autoantibody hemolysis includes drug-independent methyldopa (m/c) and procainamide, penicillin, cephalosporins and cold-reacting lenalidomide.
Immune-complex hemolysis is caused by quinidine, rifampicin and isoniazid; adsorption hemolysis is caused by high-dose penicillin (extravascular).
